citations.claim: first energy violation at step 100: total energy drifted far from initial value during close encounter
at violating step bodies are in deep close encounter with very high speed
one step before violation energy already drifting as separation shrinks
earlier at wider separation energy still near initial value

counterfactual.change: Reduced dt from 0.009904558942630679 to 0.002 with all else identical; finer resolution of the close pericenter passage removes the energy drift.

explanation: Two-body close encounter drives failure: bodies fall from separation ~4.47 to 0.50 (comparable to softening 0.3), speeds rise to ~13.5, kinetic ~651 and potential ~-783. Fixed-dt leapfrog with only 1->9 substeps cannot resolve the sharp pericenter acceleration/turnaround; energy drifts monotonically from -102.25 at step 0 to -102.19 at step 98, -113.43 at step 99, -132.23 at step 100, breaching the 2% tolerance. Reducing dt alone restores conservation, confirming timestep-resolution cause, not NaN or momentum error (momentum conserved).
vision_note: Two blue bodies move toward each other along a tight track and their separation shrinks steadily from step 97 to 100. By step 100 they are nearly overlapping in a close encounter rather than maintaining a wide stable separation.
